newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 26.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Some Walt Disney shareholders complained at the company's annual meeting about Disney's multimillion-dollar payout to former President Michael Ovitz and a pricey new contract for Chairman Michael Eisner.
* Kimberly-Clark said it would sell its three pulp mills and concentrate on its consumer products business.
* Workers have greater confidence about keeping their jobs and consumer confidence remains strong.
* Patriot American is in talks to acquire Wyndham Hotel, which has a market value of more than $600 million.
* Wal-Mart posted a 16 percent rise in quarterly profit and led other retailers whose earnings came in above analysts' estimates.
* Ford is expected to pick J.P. Morgan over Goldman Sachs to lead the initial public offering for Hertz.
* The Supreme Court ruled that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is not authorized to regulate "off-exchange" trading in options to buy or sell foreign currency.
* Dell Computer's quarterly profit more than doubled, beating analysts' estimates.
* America Online received $100 million from Tel-Save to market Tel-Save's long-distance services to AOL customers.
* Great Western created an employee severance program that could raise the cost of a takeover from H.F. Ahmanson.
* Centennial Technologies shares more than tripled after positive comments from the company's interim chief executive, but trading was halted after the company downplayed the remarks.
* Marvel Entertainment bondholders won a victory after a federal bankruptcy judge ruled that they may foreclose on the bonds and take possession of the Marvel common stock collaterizing their bonds.

* On Wall Street, they're being called the "suburban bankers." In the 1980s -- much more than today -- Wall Street's hottest investment bankers at securities firms were birds of prey, swooping from deal to deal and helping to engineer hostile takover transactions that struck fear in many of corporate America's chief executives.
But a different breed of merger masters has come back in fashion at the Wall Street firms. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bonds were little changed in the second day of lethargic trading as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on the economy today. -- Credit Markets.
